title: Olfactory and Gustatory Function in Patients with Migraine
summary:
Background
Many people with migraine perceive certain odours as unpleasant and avoid them in everyday life. It has been shown that olfactory function may deteriorate depending on the duration of the disease and the chronification of migraine. So far, it remains unclear whether there are also changes in gustatory function in people with migraine.
Research Question
The study investigates whether people with more frequent migraine attacks show poorer olfactory function over time than people with less frequent migraine attacks. In addition, it aims to examine how well people with migraine perceive taste qualities and food-related aromas.
Methodology
Participants are assessed at the beginning of the study and again after three to six months. Olfactory function is tested using odour pens. The assessment examines the concentration at which an odour is perceived, how well different odours can be distinguished, and how well familiar everyday odours can be identified.
In addition, participants complete questionnaires on migraine and everyday symptoms. At the first appointment, gustatory function is also tested using four taste sprays. Participants are asked to identify the taste qualities sweet, sour, salty, and bitter. Furthermore, the study assesses how well aromas from food powders are recognised during eating.
The results are intended to help improve the understanding of the relationship between migraine, olfactory function, and gustatory function.

interventions.name: Olfactory function will be assesd in patients with high frequent migraine  at the initial appointment and again 3–6 months later. In addition, the sense of taste is assessed once during the initial appointment.

Olfactory function will be assesd in patients with low frequent migraine  at the initial appointment and again 3–6 months later. In addition, the sense of taste is assessed once during the initial appointment.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adults with diagnosed migraine according to the criteria of the International Classification of Headache Disorders
Exclusion criteria:
Tumour diseases requiring current treatment
Mental disorders requiring current treatment
Insufficient ability to communicate adequately
